utterances.text: Do we have a sitting schedule of any kind so we have some idea of dates we are going to sit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is, first let me make the order. The Chamber, in regard to motion -- now I have misplaced the motion -- the number of the motion is -- is it this one on the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Chamber, with reference to motion by defendant Radoslav Brdjanin to delay the testimony of Mr. Robert Donia, filed on the 15th of January, 2002, having heard the parties, including also submissions made by Defence counsel to defendant General Talic, in regard to the response filed by same regarding -- to the motion by the Prosecution dated 11 January, 2002, for the filing of the report of Mr. Robert Donia as an expert witness, and having also seen the said motion of the Prosecution of the 11th January, decides to reject the motion of defendant Radoslav Brdjanin filed on the 15th of January, namely the motion to delay the testimony of Robert Donia, on the understanding that a translation into B/C/S of the report mentioned aforesaid will be filed and communicated to the Defence, to both the defendants, by not later than Friday, January the 18th. The Tribunal reserves the right to modify or decide contrario imperio on this motion should the B/C/S translation aforesaid not be filed as stated. The motion by the Prosecution dated 11th January, 2002, for the revision of expert witness Robert Donia is being acceded -- is being acceded to on the same understanding, namely, that a B/C/S translation of the report of Mr. Robert Donia be filed in the Registry of this Tribunal and be communicated to both defendants by not later than Friday the 18th of January. The trial conference stands adjourned to Monday at 9.30 in the morning, Monday, the 21st, 9.30 in the morning, with the understanding also that the trial is scheduled to start on Wednesday, 23rd, at 9.00 in the morning. And with the understanding also that if by that time the other four motions referred to -- the other four motions from defendant Brdjanin and Talic that were discussed today and that were filed yesterday would have not yet been -- would still be -- would not have been withdrawn. In the meantime, they will be decided orally on that day. So that is the understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is also the other matter that you raised, that you drew my attention to, and that is Mr. Brdjanin's motion with regard to those three or four witnesses on 92, that also will be decided orally on Wednesday morning. However, if you feel that you need time to enter a reply, I will give you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We have replied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have replied already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The motion is quite old. It was in December. And we replied almost straight away. I'm sorry, the one this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is filed today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can reply orally. Can I hand Your Honour or perhaps I can give it to Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I mean. This is the document that was filed today, and it's an objection and/or consent to Rule 92 bis witness's statement number 1. And I won't mention names, but there are one, two, three witnesses in particular, and the -- anyway, there are specific requests with regard to each.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I think Your Honour won't be able to make a decision without having the statements in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Those are 92 bis statements, I understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: These are the statements we wish to put in, and they have got the attestation. Unless there's an objection, I propose to give them to Your Honour now so Your Honour can see what's contained in them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. C'est la vie.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, they are redacted in the only way that Judge Hunt agreed, that is to say, their current whereabouts have been extracted from the statements. But if Your Honour requires them, they can be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we can call it a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm so sorry. There's one last thing. We haven't had any written or oral notification from the Defence in respect of General Talic as to the -- whether they will accept those statements. I would think it highly unlikely, but I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pitron has already told you once and twice that he is tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't accept these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then, Your Honour, I think it is better that we deal with the matter in oral submissions. Your Honour will recall that I did ask that from now on, because of the problems with the translation French/English and so on and so forth, that we deal with matters orally in Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I was going to deal with the other witness. Okay, so you -- if I give you until tomorrow to reply to this 92 bis objection filed by Mr. Ackerman today, would that be enough, or do you require more?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we can probably -- given the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm asking you to say yes to tomorrow for a very simple reason, because that would give me time to sit down with my advisors, with my legal assistants, and work on it before the weekend comes because then the weekend comes and everyone is alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I asked about General Talic's counsel, because Mr. Ackerman has given reasons why these people. They have just said no, they don't accept them. But the point is they may not accept them, but it's for Your Honour to rule. So they may want to explain why they don't accept them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you are getting used to me as yet. I don't ask these questions. My approach is you are all intelligent enough to know what the position is. He hasn't said anything. I certainly don't have to answer for any of the objections that he may have raised because he hasn't raised any. He just said, "No, I object." That's it. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand that there are actually written schedules of when we're going to be sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I seem to be the only lawyer in The Hague that doesn't have one, although nobody has been able to show me one. They don't agree with each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had every good intention -- well, I started this Pre-Trial Conference today to finish it in about two hours. Of course, I didn't know about this. I didn't know about the five motions. I didn't know about a lot of things that actually came to surface very much unexpectedly, and which were controversial. So the sitting went on much longer than I anticipated. This was one of the major matters which I had in mind of tackling. It will be done Monday. But it's very much on my mind. I have got ideas. I have also got recommendations that I will make, to make life easier for all of you and to enable you also to be able to -- to enable you to programme ahead weeks in advance. But of course, we don't have time today. But please don't go back to your hotel or where you are staying frustrated, at least on this point. Definitely this is something that will be dealt with on Monday, also because I am sure that the Prosecution also would like to know what the schedule is. But I can also tell you, be prepared for this trial to be heard in the mornings between now and March. It seems to be like that. After March, I think we'll have to switch to an afternoon. If the sixth trial doesn't start immediately, then we will explore together the possibility of perhaps utilising any space or available courtrooms that we may have. But again that's something that we need to discuss. I mean, I'm not in a position to tell you more at this point in time. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that the interpreters have had a very long day, but can I just mention, we have arranged the provisional schedule for witnesses based on the Court calendar issued on the 9th of January, which shows us sitting every morning until the end of March, bar two days which is a UN holiday and court maintenance, although they seem to think we are going to sit on Good Friday as well, which I think is unlikely. The other matter is this, Your Honour: Your Honour, if Your Honour is able to establish, and you may not be able to, the trial of Stakic, which has been, we understand from the response to the motion which I would like to revisit with Your Honour, as I think Your Honour would, next Monday morning, if we could be given some idea of when that is likely to start? For two reasons: One, it may affect how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a second and throw the ball back in your court? Tell you -- you would help me a lot in giving you an answer or in providing you with a solution if you tell me when it's likely to have the Prijedor chapter or municipality come up in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Chronologically it comes up immediately after Banja Luka. It was the first municipality to be taken over. Now, it's unfortunate but we can do -- we can put it back, but we need to put it back if there is to be any sort of connection, and that's why I need to revisit this with Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, if you tell me Banja Luka, please forgive my ignorance, but I will to have to ask you, okay, when does it start, when does it finish?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The evidence? Well, that depends very much on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Banja Luka Prosecution, Banja Luka also Defence --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what I mean. I understand that it may be the witness who is coming immediately after the investigator will be in the witness box for a week. That is -- that's the rough indication I've been given. We've effectively worked out that the Banja Luka witnesses will take us through until, at the very least, the end of February. That's our rough estimation of how long we think cross-examination will last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, we'll talk about it Monday, okay? But the Tribunal is appreciative of the problems that exist and we will try and find a solution. Also to Stakic, but no joinder. I also would like to thank the interpreters for their patience. You have been most cooperative, and this Tribunal is very appreciative.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Pre-Trial Conference adjourned at
